judgments.justification: “highest scores on all reported metrics” with “statistically significant improvements” correctly covers all five in-domain metrics and the paired p < 0.05 test.
“smaller Model M variants (40M and 42M) also outperformed all multilingual baselines on every in-domain metric” reports the finding.
It reports MRR@100, NDCG@100, and Recall@100 but omits Recall@200 and the 0.001 margin.
“possibly due to the sparse and incomplete relevance judgments” incorrectly presents judgment sparsity as a cause rather than a limitation on recall reliability.
It does not discuss random seeds, variance, exact p-values, test statistics, sample size, or sidedness.
It does not report the mixed baseline-specific pattern, model-size dependence, or gte-modernbert-base’s failure.
“statistically significant improvements…over the strongest multilingual baseline on MRR@10, NDCG@10, and Recall@10/50/100” correctly reports the finding.
“smaller Model M variants (40M and 42M) also outperform all multilingual baselines on the same in-domain metrics” reports the finding.
It covers only MRR@100 and NDCG@100, omitting both recall metrics and the near-tie at Recall@200.
“no significance markers are given” and “sparse/incomplete relevance judgments make recall-based assessments unreliable” directly report both limitations.
It does not report missing seed variation, variance estimates, or the unreported paired-test details.
It omits Model M-110M’s comparisons with gte and snowflake, model-size dependence, and gte-modernbert-base’s failure.
“highest scores on all reported metrics” with “statistically significant improvements” correctly covers the five in-domain metrics and paired p < 0.05 test.
“smaller Model M variants (40M and 42M) also outperformed all multilingual baselines on every in-domain metric” reports the finding.
It gives selected MRR@100 and Recall@100 comparisons but omits the complete four-metric e5 comparison and Recall@200 near-tie.
It reports no significance testing but omits sparse/incomplete judgments and their effect on recall reliability.
It does not discuss random seeds, variance, or the missing details of the in-domain paired tests.
Although it says performance “varied by metric and baseline,” it omits Model M-40M’s weakness, size dependence, Recall@200, and gte-modernbert-base’s failure.
